chapter: Long Island years and Battle's estate
title: Battle's big schemes and the estate
summary: Battle always wanted large sums to start and drew back from backers; the daughter and Durham consider producing his records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well, I mean, it seemed to me from the time when I first met Edgar Battle, he was always talking about things like this, but nothing ever happened.
Because he would get right to the door and close it. He(inaudible) say, "I got to have a million dollars."
"I got to have $400,000 dollars or I can't do this," instead of taking a little bit and trying to condense it down. Everything was --
Yeah. And the guys would back off of it, the backers, (inaudible). They'd get right to the door and
then back up. They'd ask for, say, a percentage. "No, I ain't giving you nothing," and that was it. He didn't want to give up nothing.
Well, he was an oddball though, because he always seemed confident. I don't know whether that was just an act, but --
-- I mean, you'd meet him on the street, he was always -- chest out and. So, I mean, what have you got to do now with the estate?

Well, the daughter must have planned to probably go ahead and open up the firm and maybe try to collect some of the money, but I told her right then she might never get it (inaudible). What you got to do is just take advantage of the company. Maybe I make some records, might produce them and throw them in there. She said she was willing to put up six or $7,000 behind sessions or something. I'm saying we can produce a product, finish it and peddle it. You understand? If it's good enough, you might get rid of it.
Well, the proposition is to record some of his music?

Record it and record what I got to the best of my knowledge with something new in a band or something -- eight or nine, ten pieces (inaudible). Maybe with singers. We got singers, and try to produce a product and try to unload
Well, what about all the records he's got made?
That's what I said. The things he's made, he got some good things made. They can be edited. He's got finished stuff there, plenty of it.
Well, it seems to me that would be the first thing to work on (inaudible).
(Inaudible) and he's got an outlet in France, I know.
I don't know whether that's anything in Africa or not.
